R371.note: Closes the short-read gap by rejecting any Read that returns fewer than 8 bytes, but the right shape for a Stream.Read sink is to fill the buffer (loop or ReadAtLeast/ReadExactly) rather than reject on a partial read; the inputs newly rejected (under-8-byte files, transient short reads) are not valid uploads in practice and the check is stated.

R372.note: Function constructor is replaced by expr-eval-fork Parser, which closes code execution, but ast.evaluate(order) binds the variables as total/tax rather than order, so the contract's own example order.total + order.tax throws 'undefined variable: order' (expr-eval resolves IVAR against the values object) while the write-up claims the contract is preserved - legitimate previews silently break.

R373.note: Strict in_array allowlist of the four public verbs before the dynamic dispatch; all documented macros still work and nothing else changes.

R374.note: parseClaimsJws with a bound SecretKey rejects alg:none and unsigned tokens on jjwt 0.11.5; the new constructor parameter and the catch-and-continue-unauthenticated behaviour are both stated plainly and block no legitimate caller (deprecated Jwts.parser()/setSigningKey still function on 0.11.5).

R375.note: HMAC-then-restricted-unpickle is the right shape when the pickled model object must be kept, but until the out-of-scope batch job appends signatures every existing cache entry now fails with 500 (stated as a required follow-up), and the hardcoded 'default-dev-key' fallback plus a broad __main__/numpy/sklearn find_class allowlist are questionable constructs.

R376.note: SIZE_MAX / sizeof(ProductRow) guard before the multiplication, freeing batch on the reject path; valid counts and the NULL-on-failure contract are unchanged.

R377.note: realpath plus separator-aware str_starts_with containment before file_get_contents, 404 on failure matching the original's missing-file response; note the base directory itself is not realpath'd, which would reject everything only if /var/www/reports were a symlink.

R378.note: Signature verification with a pinned HS256 algorithm closes the forgery, but the shipped code verifies against a hardcoded placeholder 'your-secret-key-here' (rejecting every real token until configured, stated as a follow-up), and only InvalidSignatureError/DecodeError are caught so missing-claim, expired or wrong-algorithm tokens now surface as 500 instead of the original 401.

R379.note: Clean plus HasPrefix with a trailing separator (and exact-root equality) confines the joined path to docsRoot; only escaping inputs see the new 403, legitimate names are served as before.

R380.note: Resulting code uses prepareStatement with a ? placeholder and setString, which is the correct API, but the case was already written that way - the diff is empty and the write-up's claim that the original concatenated input into the SQL string is inaccurate.

R381.note: Tika.detect(Path) replaces the extension-driven probeContentType with content magic detection against the same allowlist; tika-core dependency and the new IOException 500 path are stated, and genuine JPEG/PNG/PDF uploads still pass.

R382.note: html.escape replaces Markup on the caller-supplied label, so it renders as text; output for benign labels is the same visible text and nothing else changes.

R383.note: prepare with ? placeholder and execute([$sku]) replaces the concatenated query; false-from-prepare/execute still maps to the original null/404 path.

R384.note: Allowlisted field mapped into an ORM icontains lookup with tenant_id bound closes the identifier injection, but the five allowed columns (email/phone/company/address) are invented rather than taken from the model or stated as needing reconciliation, so an approved field outside that set now raises an uncaught ValueError, and icontains escapes % and _ that the original ILIKE passed through as wildcards.

R385.note: resolve_entities=False on the XMLParser stops entity substitution so external entities are never fetched; ordinary orderId/note documents parse exactly as before (documents relying on internal DTD entities would see them unexpanded, intrinsic to this standard fix).

R386.note: Checks the boolean from SignedJWT.verify and throws JOSEException on false, so claims are only read after a valid RSA signature; valid tokens behave exactly as before.
